segments.text: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure. Iceland volcano erupts again on the Reykjanes peninsula. Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line. Good evening, and welcome to WORLD NOW. I'm Paco Pixel, with Lola Byte.
Breaking news. In Panama, the canal authority says about 30 ships are waiting to cross. The Panama Canal has reopened to ships after fog closed it for a day, according to Ledger Line.
segments.headline: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure

segments.text: A fissure eruption has started again on the Reykjanes peninsula in Iceland, Pixelburg Post reports. Scientists say lava is flowing away from nearby towns and flights are not affected.
segments.headline: Iceland volcano erupts again on the Reykjanes peninsula

segments.text: Thanks, Lola. Our number of the day: 40,000. Lisbon has opened a new tram line along the Tagus river, according to Pixelburg Post. The city says the 9 kilometre route will carry 40,000 passengers a day and cut car traffic in the old town. As the mayor put it: “This line will change how people move around the old town.”
segments.headline: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line

quote.text: This line will change how people move around the old town

segments.text: Now, around the world in 30 seconds. In Kerala, local authorities have opened 120 relief camps and closed schools for two days, Pixelburg Post reports.
segments.headline: Heavy rain floods streets in coastal towns of Kerala

segments.text: Venice has raised its sea barriers for a test ahead of the autumn high tides, according to Bitport Herald.
segments.headline: Venice raises its sea barriers in a test before the autumn tides

segments.text: In Morocco, its operator says it supplies electricity for more than 1 million people.
segments.headline: Morocco desert solar plant reaches full power

segments.text: In China, the cost of shipping a container from Shanghai to Rotterdam has fallen by 20 percent in a month.
segments.headline: Shipping costs fall as port congestion eases

segments.text: And finally: Scientists say coral cover has grown on parts of the Great Barrier Reef for a second year. “The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break,” a lead researcher said.
segments.headline: Coral recovers on parts of the Great Barrier Reef

quote.text: The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break

segments.text: Good to hear the sea is having a better day than most of us.
Low bar. But we will take it.
That's WORLD NOW. From Lola Byte and from me, thank you for watching. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24.
